faq.contact: Still unsure? Talk to us on <discord>Discord</discord>, <telegram>Telegram</telegram> or <email>hello@tokhive.ai</email>.

vendor.question: How do I know the tokens really come from the official vendor?
vendor.answer: Every request is relayed from inside an AMD SEV-SNP confidential VM that can only open TLS connections to official vendor endpoints. Each response carries a signed attestation report (application measurement, upstream host and response hash) that you can check with our open-source verifier.

credentials.question: Can TokHive or other users see my credentials or prompts?
credentials.answer: Bee encrypts upstream credentials with the TEE public key before uploading them. Hive processes buyer requests for routing and execution, and failure diagnostics can retain request and response content. Providers do not see buyer content through Bee's encrypted relay.

earn.question: How much can I earn as a provider?
earn.answer: Earnings depend on your available quota, provider rates and the requests you successfully serve. Each request is settled individually, and you can review your settled earnings in the dashboard.

usage.question: Will sharing affect my own usage?
usage.answer: Sharing uses your subscription quota. You can stop sharing at any time when you need that quota for your own requests.

prices.question: How are prices set?
prices.answer: Prices are set at a discount to the official vendor prices. The discount is adjusted periodically based on supply and demand.

tools.question: Which tools and SDKs work with TokHive?
tools.answer: Tools that use the OpenAI Responses or Chat Completions API, or the Anthropic Messages API: Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, Cursor, the official SDKs, LangChain and more. You only change the base URL and the API key. The docs list the supported features.

settlement.question: How do settlement and withdrawals work?
settlement.answer: Earnings are credited to your earnings balance in real time as each successful request settles. Withdraw from your wallet in Web3 stablecoins, with a $10 minimum and a network fee based on the actual on-chain cost. You can review per-request settlement records in your dashboard.

steps.title: Three steps to your first earnings.

signIn.title: Sign in locally
signIn.description: Sign in to your subscription account on your computer. Bee encrypts your credentials with the TEE public key before uploading them. Only the TEE can decrypt them; nobody at TokHive can see your credentials in plaintext.

share.title: Start sharing with Bee
share.description: Run Bee on your computer and keep it connected to share your subscription quota. You can start or stop sharing at any time.

earn.title: Earn in real time

protections.title: Your account stays in your hands.

stop.label: OFF SWITCH
stop.title: Stop Bee, and nothing runs
stop.description: The TEE can reach the vendor only through a connection that your running Bee relays. When Bee is stopped, no request can run on your account, and the credential it uploaded lapses when the access token expires.

local.label: CREDENTIALS
local.title: Your refresh token stays on your computer
local.description: Bee uploads only the access token, sealed to the TEE. The refresh token stays in the official client's local store, so renewing access always happens on your machine.

open.label: SOFTWARE
open.title: Open source, with a fixed list of hosts
open.description: Bee is MIT-licensed and public on GitHub, so you can read it or build it yourself. It connects only to Hive and to the vendor endpoints on its allowlist, and it relays buyer traffic as encrypted bytes it cannot read.

risks.vendor: TokHive is not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic or OpenAI. Their terms may not allow sharing a subscription, and a vendor can limit, suspend or close an account that is shared. That risk is yours, and TokHive does not compensate for a lost or restricted subscription.
risks.rejection: If a vendor rejects or rate-limits an account, Hive stops sending it new requests. Requests in progress may fail; failed requests earn nothing, and earnings already settled stay in your balance. TokHive can also pause or ban an account from supply, for example after repeated upstream rejections or a policy violation.

encrypted.title: Credentials encrypted before upload
encrypted.description: Bee encrypts upstream access credentials with the TEE public key. Only the TEE can decrypt the uploaded envelope.

aup.title: Bound by the Acceptable Use Policy
aup.description: Buyers agree to the Acceptable Use Policy, and keys that break it can be revoked.

limits.title: Per-account limits

audit.title: Full audit trail

settlement.lead: Each successful request credits your earnings balance as it settles. Withdraw from your wallet in Web3 stablecoins, with a $10 minimum withdrawal and a network fee based on the actual on-chain cost.

idle.question: What does "idle quota" mean?
idle.answer: Idle quota is unused capacity in your subscription. You choose when to share it by starting or stopping sharing.

slower.question: Will my own requests ever be slower or blocked?
slower.answer: They can be. Shared requests draw on the same subscription quota and rate limits as your own, and none of it is reserved for you. Bee keeps taking requests until a quota window is fully used, and then your own requests wait for that window to reset too. To keep quota for yourself, pause sharing with bee pause while you work and run bee resume when you are done.

stop.question: Can I stop at any time?
stop.answer: Yes. Pause sharing from Bee on your computer with the bee pause command, and start again with bee resume. Stopping sharing does not affect earnings already settled.

withdraw.question: When are earnings settled, and how do I withdraw them?
withdraw.answer: Each successful request is settled in real time and credited to your earnings balance. Withdraw from your wallet in Web3 stablecoins, with a $10 minimum and a network fee based on the actual on-chain cost. Settlement does not wait for your balance to reach the withdrawal minimum.

calculated.question: How are earnings calculated?
calculated.answer: For each billing item, such as input, output and cached tokens, your quote is the model's base price multiplied by your quote factor. You can keep the platform default factor or set your own in the Console. Buyers pay your quote, TokHive takes its commission from it, and you earn the rest. Requests go to the lowest available quote first, so a higher factor earns more per token but may serve fewer requests. The calculator above uses illustrative assumptions.

credits.question: Can sharing use my paid ChatGPT credits?
credits.answer: Yes. When an OpenAI account has used up its subscription window but still has paid credits, Hive keeps sending it requests and OpenAI charges those credits. It stops when the credits run out or reach your overage limit. Pause sharing if you do not want your credits used. Claude accounts are not affected.

apiKey.question: Can I also share an OpenAI API key?
apiKey.answer: Yes. Bee can offer an OpenAI Platform API key as fallback supply when subscription accounts are busy. The key is encrypted for the TEE like your subscription credentials. OpenAI bills you for that usage, while you earn your usual quote less the platform commission, which can be less than OpenAI charges you, especially for cache writes and long-context requests that OpenAI prices higher. You set the key's concurrency and can pause it in the Console.

registered.question: Someone has already registered my subscription account. What can I do?
registered.answer: Each subscription account can be shared by only one TokHive account, on a first-come basis. If yours was registered by someone else, contact hello@tokhive.ai. Once we have verified that you control the account, we can release it so you can register it.

computer.question: Do I need to keep my computer on?
computer.answer: Yes. Keep your computer on, connected to the internet and running Bee while sharing. Your computer must stay awake; while it is asleep or offline, it cannot receive new requests.

verify.title: Check any response in one command.

requestId.title: Grab the request ID
requestId.description: Use the X-Request-Id header returned by your TokHive API call.

run.title: Run the verifier
run.description: The verifier checks the AMD SEV-SNP report, AWS NitroTPM evidence and the signing-key binding.

measurement.title: Compare the measurement
measurement.description: The snp-app: identity must match the SHA-256 digest of the expected application bundle.

upstream.title: Check the upstream
upstream.description: The signed upstream host must match the expected vendor endpoint.

verify.instructions: Run make build in the verifier repository first. Set HIVE_API_KEY to your buyer API key, HIVE_REQUEST_ID to your request ID, and HIVE_EXPECTED_APP to the production snp-app:{sha} identity from the signed release catalog below. This example checks Anthropic's upstream host and compares the exact upstream response body saved as response.raw.

release.title: Know which TEE image to expect.
release.lead: Each TEE release and each environment it runs in is recorded in a signed release catalog. Take the expected application identity from that catalog, not from the receipt you are checking, and check the catalog's signature against the key on this page before you trust it.
release.note: This page is the independent channel for the production signing key; staging pre-releases use a different key. Compare it with the release-signing.pub attached to each release; do not trust a key read from the release assets alone. A valid signature shows who published the catalog, not what is running now; the hardware evidence in your receipt shows that.

hero.lead: Route individual TCP sessions through residential connections shared by TokHive hosts. Pick an exit by country, network type and measured quality, prepay a session, and connect with a standard HTTPS proxy — no client to install.

notice.title: What experimental means here.
notice.lead: Residential egress is in a limited rollout while we calibrate coverage, pricing and abuse controls. Use it for evaluation and low-stakes automation, never for traffic that must not fail.

items.relay: Relay mode only: traffic always passes through TokHive's gateway. Direct host endpoints are not available.
items.sla: No SLA. Coverage, latency and exit IPs change as hosts join and leave.
items.changes: Features, limits and prices can change or be withdrawn without notice.

steps.title: From catalog to home IP in four steps.

catalog.title: Pick an exit
catalog.description: Browse the catalog by country, network type and minimum quality score. Prices are listed per session; the exact IP appears only once you hold the lease.

prepay.title: Prepay a session
prepay.description: Buy 1–24 blocks in one call. Payment comes from your withdrawable balance, and the price is locked when the lease is created.

connect.title: Connect
connect.description: Send a standard HTTP CONNECT to the gateway with your egress key. curl, browsers and SDKs work without a plugin.

exit.title: Exit from home
exit.description: The host's Bee dials your target over its home line. Your TLS stays end to end; the host only forwards bytes it cannot read.

protocol.title: An HTTPS proxy, nothing proprietary.
protocol.lead: Buyers send HTTP/1.1 CONNECT to the gateway over TLS, authorized with an egress key as a bearer token. The response is a raw tunnel to the target.
protocol.note: Port 443 is allowed by default; port 80 is opt-in and warns that it is plaintext. Ports such as 22, 25, 445 and 3389 are refused, and IP literals or private ranges are rejected after DNS resolution.

pricing.title: One unit: the session block.
pricing.lead: Egress is prepaid, metered in session blocks and billed from your withdrawable balance. There is no hourly rate, no postpaid usage and no refund path.
pricing.note: Illustrative launch price. Rates differ by market and can change during the experimental period.

block.label: Session block
block.detail: 5 minutes and 16 MiB of forwarded traffic.

units.label: Blocks per lease
units.detail: Time and byte caps scale linearly; the lease ends when either runs out.

payment.label: Payment
payment.detail: Charged from withdrawable balance at lease creation. Promotional credits cannot be used.

concurrency.label: Concurrency
concurrency.detail: Up to 16 streams per lease. Batch creation covers many exits at once.

refund.label: Refunds
refund.detail: Releasing a lease ends it; unused time expires. Platform-side outages are credited by support.

ports.label: Ports
ports.detail: Port 80 opt-in with a plaintext warning; sensitive ports are blocked.

visibility.title: Who can see what.
visibility.lead: TLS runs between your client and the target, so neither TokHive nor the host can read the payload. The host never learns who you are.
visibility.note: Hostnames and byte counts are kept for 30 days for abuse review, then reduced to salted hashes. The host sees the target hostname during the lease, never your account, key or payload.

tcp.title: TCP only
tcp.description: v1 is HTTP CONNECT over TCP. UDP, QUIC and SOCKS5 UDP associate are out of scope.

ports.title: A narrow port policy
ports.description: 443 by default, 80 on request. Mail, SSH, SMB, RDP, Redis and similar ports are refused.

private.title: No private networks
private.description: Loopback, RFC1918, CGNAT, link-local and IPv4-mapped IPv6 targets are rejected after resolution.

sla.title: Not a guarantee
sla.description: TokHive measures and signs the exit at lease start, but a probe is not proof of every packet's path.

experimental.question: Why is this labelled experimental?
experimental.answer: Relay mode works, but coverage, host supply and abuse tooling are still being calibrated. Expect gaps, and do not put production traffic on it yet.

anonymous.question: Is this an anonymity service?
anonymous.answer: No. Buyers are verified, targets are logged and the acceptable use policy applies. Egress gives you a residential source IP, not anonymity.

udp.question: Can I send UDP?
udp.answer: Not today. CONNECT carries TCP streams only; UDP would need a separate MASQUE endpoint and is not part of this release.

offline.question: What happens if a host disconnects?
offline.answer: The lease is interrupted. Prepaid time is not refunded, though platform-side failures are credited when attributable. Use the batch endpoint to spread long jobs across several exits.

refund.question: Why are sessions non-refundable?
refund.answer: Each block costs a fraction of a cent, so a refund path would cost more than it returns and invite abuse. Buy the number of blocks the job needs.

access.question: How do I get access?
access.answer: Sign in to the console, add a withdrawable balance and create a lease. Experimental access may be limited by region or account review.

cta.title: Try it on one session.
cta.lead: One block is five minutes and a fraction of a cent. Start with a single exit, then scale with batches.

notice.lead: We are calibrating ISP compliance, abuse handling and payouts with a small group of hosts. Applications are reviewed manually, and egress mode can be paused for a host or a region at any time.

steps.title: Opt in, set limits, stay in control.

optin.title: Turn on egress
optin.description: Residential mode is a separate switch in Bee, off by default and independent of token sharing. Turn it off whenever you want.

limits.title: Set your limits
limits.description: Choose concurrent streams, a bandwidth cap and allowed ports. Bee enforces them locally, not just at the gateway.

tokens.title: Approve each lease
tokens.description: Every lease carries a short-lived token signed by TokHive, bound to your device and the policy hash. Bee verifies it before dialing anything.

earn.title: Get paid per session
earn.description: Completed session blocks are credited to your earnings balance. Failed dials and platform-rejected targets pay nothing.

lan.label: LAN
lan.title: Private ranges are refused
lan.description: Loopback, RFC1918, CGNAT, link-local and IPv4-mapped IPv6 targets are rejected after DNS resolution. Buyers cannot reach your router or devices.

tls.label: CONTENT
tls.title: Bytes stay encrypted
tls.description: Buyers run TLS to the target through your line. You forward ciphertext and cannot read or modify it.

tokens.label: LEASES
tokens.title: Signed, short-lived tokens
tokens.description: Each lease is authorized by a short-lived token bound to one policy version and checked locally by Bee.

identity.label: IDENTITY
identity.title: No buyer identity
identity.description: You never see the buyer's account, key or contact details. The console shows lease counts and bytes, not people.

switch.label: KILL SWITCH
switch.title: Stop instantly
switch.description: Stopping Bee or the egress switch closes every open stream at once and rejects new leases.

open.label: SOFTWARE
open.title: Open source
open.description: Bee is MIT-licensed and public, so the policy enforcement you rely on can be read and built from source.

earnings.title: Paid per completed session.
earnings.lead: Each finished block is credited to your earnings balance and stays pending for 30 days to cover ISP complaints and abuse review. After that it can be withdrawn normally.

items.session: Each completed block is credited at the listed price, less platform commission.
items.holdback: 30-day holdback, then withdraw through the existing wallet.
items.payout: Failed dials and platform-rejected targets earn nothing and cost you nothing.

statement.title: STATEMENT · EXPERIMENTAL
statement.note: Sample only, at the launch block price. Volume depends on demand in your country and network; there is no minimum or guaranteed amount.

requirements.title: What hosting takes.
requirements.lead: Hosts are reviewed before egress is enabled. The line must be yours to share, and the machine must stay online while you host.

line.title: A residential line
line.description: A home broadband connection with spare upload. Metered, mobile or shared building links are reviewed case by case.

region.title: A supported country
region.description: Coverage is limited to markets where we have calibrated ISP terms and abuse handling.

isp.title: An ISP that allows it
isp.description: Check your contract first. Running a proxy can breach residential terms, and that risk stays with you.

bee.title: Bee on a machine you control
bee.description: Bee must stay connected while hosting. Egress mode runs alongside token sharing without changing it.

risks.title: Know what you are taking on.

items.experimental: Experimental terms: features, rates and eligibility can change, and egress mode can be paused for your host or region.
items.availability: Availability events such as disconnects, IP changes and ISP maintenance reduce earnings and are recorded against your host.
items.abuse: An abuse complaint about a buyer can suspend your egress while we investigate and withhold settlement for the affected period.

risks.isp: Your ISP contract governs this. Some residential providers prohibit proxies or resale of connectivity, and TokHive cannot defend an account on your behalf.
risks.consent: Enabling egress requires an explicit confirmation in Bee and the console. It is never switched on by token sharing, updates or defaults.

what.question: What exactly do buyers get?
what.answer: A TCP session that exits from your residential IP, limited to allowlisted ports and bounded by time and bytes. Not a VPN, not your device, not your account.

when.question: When can I host?
when.answer: Applications are reviewed manually during the experimental period. Token providers in supported regions are considered first.

howmuch.question: How much can I earn?
howmuch.answer: It depends on demand in your country, your upload capacity and how long you host. The block price is the most a session can earn; income is not guaranteed.

safe.question: Can buyers see my files or devices?
safe.answer: No. Egress carries one TCP stream to a public target. Private ranges are blocked after resolution, and the payload stays inside the buyer's TLS.

stop.question: How do I stop?
stop.answer: Switch egress off in Bee or the console. Open streams close immediately, and pending earnings are unaffected.
